facts.statement: The genus Sahitisuchus was named by Kellner, Pinheiro, and Campos in 2014.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus was named by Alexander W. A. Kellner, André E. P. Pinheiro and Diogenes A. Campos in 2014

facts.statement: The generic name honors the Xavante people, an indigenous group from Brazil.
facts.quote: The generic name honors the Xavante people, one of the indigenous Brazilian inhabitants.

facts.statement: The species is known only from a single nearly complete skull and lower jaw, along with several neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus is known solely from the holotype MCT 1730-R, a nearly complete skull and lower jaw, proatlas, an intercentrum, the axis and the third cervical vertebra

facts.statement: The fossil was found during a five-decade exploration of the São José de Itaboraí Basin that concluded in 1984.
facts.quote: MCT 1730-R was discovered during the exploration of the São José de Itaboraí Basin, located in Rio de Janeiro State, that lasted for about five decades and ended in 1984.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the late Itaboraian age of the Early Eocene, approximately 53 to 50 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating to the late Itaboraian South American land mammals age of the Early Eocene, about 53-50 million years ago.

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus was primarily terrestrial but may have lived a semi-aquatic lifestyle to some extent.
facts.quote: It is a terrestrial sebecid, although it may also have adopted a semi-aquatic lifestyle to some degree

facts.statement: It has two unique traits among sebecids: a fused odontoid process lacking medial processes and a mandible without an external fenestra.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus possesses the two following autapomorphies among sebecids: the odontoid process is fused to the axis with vertical anterior surface, lacking medial processes, and its mandible lacks an external mandibular fenestra.

facts.statement: The skull is elongated with slight constrictions near the fifth and eleventh maxillary tooth sockets.
facts.quote: The skull of Sahitisuchus is elongated in dorsal view, showing two slight constrictions at about the level of the fifth and eleventh maxillary alveoli

facts.statement: Its snout is flatter and less domed than those of related genera like Sebecus and Barinasuchus.
facts.quote: The snout of Sahitisuchus is not as tall and domed (oreinirostral) as seen in Sebecus, Barinasuchus, Bretesuchus, Zulmasuchus and Langstonia.

facts.statement: It had 12 maxillary teeth with blunt posterior teeth, a feature shared with other Paleogene sebecosuchians.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus possesses 12 maxillary teeth, similarly to 10 maxillary teeth in other Paleogene sebecosuchians (Lorosuchus, Bretesuchus and Zulmasuchus), as well as blunt posterior teeth, unlike Cretaceous sebecosuchians.

facts.statement: It is classified as an extinct genus of sebecid mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus is an extinct genus of sebecid mesoeucrocodylian

facts.statement: The animal belongs to the family Sebecidae.
facts.quote: familia: Sebecidae

facts.statement: It lived in the Rio de Janeiro state in southeastern Brazil during the Paleocene.
facts.quote: que vivió en el Estado de Río de Janeiro en el sureste de Brasil durante el Paleoceno.

facts.statement: The holotype was briefly mentioned in 1946, 1991, and 1993 but was not formally described until 2014.
facts.quote: MCT 1730-R was briefly mentioned in the literature by Price and Paula-Couto (1946) and later in 1991 and 1993, but had never been figured or described before Kellner et al. (2014) assigned it to a new genus and species.

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus is one of only two species formally described from the São José de Itaboraí Basin.
facts.quote: Apart from Sahitisuchus fluminensis, Eocaiman itaboraiensis is the only other species formally described based on remains collected at São José de Itaboraí Basin.

facts.statement: The genus Sahitisuchus was named by Alexander W. A. Kellner, André E. P. Pinheiro, and Diogenes A. Campos in 2014.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus fue nombrado por Alexander W. A. Kellner, André E. P. Pinheiro y Diogenes A. Campos en 2014

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Xavante people, an indigenous group from Brazil.
facts.quote: El nombre del género honra a los xavantes, uno de los pueblos indígenas del Brasil.

facts.statement: The species name fluminensis is a Latinization of fluminense, referring to citizens of the state of Rio de Janeiro.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, fluminensis, es una latinización de fluminense, el gentilicio usado para los ciudadanos del Estado de Río de Janeiro.

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus is known only from holotype MCT 1730-R, which includes an almost complete skull, mandible, proatlas, intercentrum, axis, and third vertebra.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus es conocido únicamente a partir del holotipo MCT 1730-R, un cráneo casi completo y la mandíbula, el proatlas, un intercentrum, el axis y la tercera vértebra

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered during an exploration of the São José de Itaboraí Basin in Rio de Janeiro that lasted nearly five decades and ended in 1984.
facts.quote: MCT 1730-R fue descubierto durante una exploración de la Cuenca São José de Itaboraí, localizada en el estado de Río de Janeiro, que duró cerca de cinco décadas y finalizó en 1984.

facts.statement: The holotype was briefly mentioned in literature in 1946, 1991, and 1993 but was not described until Kellner et al. assigned it to a new genus and species in 2014.
facts.quote: MCT 1730-R fue brevemente mencionado en la literatura por Price y Paula-Couto (1946) y más tarde en 1991 y 1993, pero nunca había sido mostrado ni descrito antes de que Kellner et al. (2014) lo asignaran a un nuevo género y especie.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the late Itaboraiense age of South America, corresponding to the mid-Late Paleocene, approximately 56.5 to 58.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: que data de finales de la edad biocronológica Itaboraiense de Suramérica que corresponde a mediados del Paleoceno Superior, hace unos 56.5-58.2 millones de años.

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus is a sebecosuchian crocodylomorph, representing a primitive form found alongside more derived Alligatoridae in the Paleocene.
facts.quote: A la fecha, este es el único depósito del Paleoceno en donde la fauna de crocodilomorfos estaba compuesta por una forma más bien primitiva (Sahitisuchus, un sebecosuquio) y otra más derivada (Alligatoridae) tras la extinción masiva del Cretácico-Terciario.

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus possesses two autapomorphies among sebecids: the odontoid process fuses to the axis with a vertical anterior surface, lacks medial processes, and its mandible lacks an external fenestra.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus posee las dos siguientes autapomorfias entre los sebécidos: el proceso odontoide se fusiona al axis con una superficie anterior vertical, carece de procesos mediales, y su mandíbula carece de una fenestra externa.

facts.statement: Like Lorosuchus, Sahitisuchus has a shallow ventrolateral depression in the infraorbital region of the jugal bone.
facts.quote: Como en Lorosuchus, tiene una depresión poco profunda ventrolateral en la región infraorbital del hueso yugal.

facts.statement: The jugal of Sahitisuchus is very large and ornamented, with a posterior ramus higher than the anterior process that expands laterally, a feature previously seen only in Bretesuchus.
facts.quote: El yugal de Sahitisuchus es muy grande y ornamentado, como fue observado con anterioridad solamente en Bretesuchus, su ramo posterior es más alto que el proceso anterior y se expande lateralmente.

facts.statement: Like many basal mesoeucrocodylian taxa including sebecosuchians, Sahitisuchus possesses a longitudinal frontal crest.
facts.quote: Como en muchos taxones de mesoeucrocodilianos basales, como los sebecosuquios Lorosuchus, Sebecus, Zulmasuchus, Iberosuchus y Pepesuchus, posee una cresta longitudinal frontal.

facts.statement: In Sahitisuchus, the frontal crest is low and smooth, running from the middle to the posterior part of the frontal bone.
facts.quote: En Sahitisuchus, esta es baja y lisa, corriendo desde la parte media a la parte posterior del frontal.

facts.statement: Like all sebecid species, the quadratojugal forms a "double articulation" by participating in the craniomandibular joint.
facts.quote: Como en todas las especies de sebécidos y algunos otros taxones no tan cercanamente relacionados, el cuadratoyugal forma una "doble articulación" al participar en la articulación cráneo-mandibular.

facts.statement: Like the peirosaurids Hamadasuchus and Lomasuchus, Sahitisuchus possesses a postdirecting squamosal protuberance that does not form a "horn".
facts.quote: Como en los peirosáuridos Hamadasuchus y Lomasuchus, Sahitisuchus posee una protuberancia del escamosal que se dirige hacia atrás y sin formar un "cuerno".

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus has only two openings in the tympanic cavity area, similar to Sebecus, Hamadasuchus, and recent species.
facts.quote: En Sahitisuchus solo hay dos aberturas, como se ve en Sebecus, Hamadasuchus y las especies recientes.

facts.statement: Compared to Sebecus, Sahitisuchus had more robust and wide diapophyses, and the length of the third cervical centrum is nearly equal to that of the axis.
facts.quote: En comparación a Sebecus, Sahitisuchus tenía diapófisis más robustas y anchas, y la longitud del centro de la tercera vértebra cervical es casi igual a la del axis.

facts.statement: The skull of Sahitisuchus is elongated in dorsal view with two slight constrictions near the fifth to eleventh maxillary alveoli, being shorter than Sebecus and Stolokrosuchus but not as short as Lorosuchus.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Sahitisuchus es alargado en vista dorsal, mostrando dos leves contricciones cerca del nivel de quinto al undécimo alvéolos maxilares, siendo comparativamente más corto que el cráneo de Sebecus y Stolokrosuchus, pero no tan corto como en Lorosuchus.

facts.statement: The snout of Sahitisuchus is not as high and domed (oreinirostre) as seen in Sebecus, Barinasuchus, Bretesuchus, Zulmasuchus, and Langstonia.
facts.quote: El hocico de Sahitisuchus no es tan alto y abovedado (oreinirostre) como se observa en Sebecus, Barinasuchus, Bretesuchus, Zulmasuchus y Langstonia.

facts.statement: The cranial vault of Sahitisuchus is flat and rectangular, being wider than it is long.
facts.quote: La bóveda craneal de Sahitisuchus es plana y rectangular, siendo más ancha que larga.

facts.statement: The supratemporal fossa is much larger than the supratemporal fenestra and is about three times smaller than the eye orbits.
facts.quote: La fosa supratemporal es mucha más grande que la fenestra supratemporal y es cerca de tres veces más pequeña que las órbitas oculares.

facts.statement: The eye orbit is situated more laterally, as in terrestrial sebecids, and not laterodorsally as in semiaquatic crocodylomorphs like Stolokrosuchus, Lorosuchus, and modern Crocodilia species.
facts.quote: La órbita ocular se sitúa más alteralmente, como en los sebécidos terrestres, y no laterodorsalmente como en los crocodiliformes semiacuáticos, como Stolokrosuchus, Lorosuchus y las especies modernas de Crocodilia.

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus possesses 12 maxillary teeth, similar to the 10 maxillary teeth of other Paleogene sebecosuchians, and has blunt posterior teeth, unlike Cretaceous sebecosuchians.
facts.quote: Sahitisuchus posee 12 dientes maxilares, similar a los 10 dientes maxilares de otros sebecosuquios del Paleógeno (Lorosuchus, Bretesuchus y Zulmasuchus), así como dientes posteriores romos, a diferencia de los sebecosuquios del Cretácico.

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus belongs to the family Sebecidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Sebecidae

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Sahitisuchus lived from the Thanetian to the Ypresian stages, between 59.24 and 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Thanetian to Ypresian (59.24 to 48.07 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ruiz et al. (2026) used a digital reconstruction to restore the fractured mandible of the holotype, demonstrating its utility for identifying morphological characters significant in phylogenetic studies.
facts.quote: Ruiz et al. (2026) present a digital reconstruction of the mandible of Sahitisuchus fluminensis, restore the original morphology of the fractured mandible of the holotype specimen, and report evidence of utility of repaired mandible for identification of morphological characters with significance in phylogenetic studies.

rejected.statement: The name combines the Xavante words for 'angry' or 'brave' warriors with the Greek name for the Egyptian crocodile god.
rejected.quote: It is derived from sahi ti, meaning 'to be angry' or 'to be brave' in Xavante language, alluding at warriors, and suchus, Latinized from the Greek souchos, an Egyptian crocodile god.
